title: Declare S7 imports and update package hooks
description:
Marquee declares S7 in Imports and uses its APIs when registering ggplot2 methods, but NAMESPACE does not import from S7. Add an explicit `S7_inherits` import in the roxygen package declarations and regenerate NAMESPACE to remove the dependency check note.

Use the S7 load, build, and unload hooks when exported by the installed S7. Unloading removes this package's dependency hooks and owned methods on external S7 generics. The existing S7 version requirement is preserved. Method registration follows the existing deferred load work.

title: Add "Supported By Posit" badge to marquee website
description:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the marquee website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

## Changes

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file
- Standardized indentation in `_pkgdown.yml`

title: Outlines
description:
This PR aims to fix #60.

Briefly, it adds the `style(outline, outline_size)` arguments and the `{.out ...}` custom span to generate outlined text.

In some more detail: it places an outline of the text underneath the regular text. For polygon-mode this is another `pathGrob()` and for glyph-mode this a `strokeGrob()`. Because it is placed underneath and the text on top follows the stroke midline, the `outline_size` is doubled for the correct effective linewidth of the stroke. 

A few unresolved issues:

* I haven't come up with a raster equivalent of outlined text. I'm not sure how often it occurs that glyphs have to be rendered as rasters, but if that is very seldomly, it shouldn't be too much of a problem.
* I haven't found a way to test this new feature. I could add a `.out` span to `markdown_test` and update snapshots, but the `.png` snapshot in the test is generated on MacOS and I only got access to Windows at the moment.
* Weirdly, the polygon-mode looks better than the `strokeGrob()` mode on the ragg device. I suspect this is some kind of pixel-snapping shenanigans that applies to glyphs but not to `strokeGrob()`s of glyphs. It can be see in the reprex, for example in the top part of the 'b' where the left vertical stroke is ~1px wide and the right vertical stroke is noticably thicker.

An example with the new span:

``` r
devtools::load_all("~/packages/test/marquee/")
#> ℹ Loading marquee
library(grid)

txt <- "Here {.out be outlined} text"
mq <- marquee_grob(txt, x = 0.5, y = 0.5, hjust = 0.5, width = NA, style = classic_style(32))
grid.newpage()
grid.draw(mq)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/QL33pfJ.png)<!-- -->

title: Flexible size for `element_marquee()` depending on margins
description:
This PR aims to fix #57.

Briefly, the issue can be summarised as that we give the instruction to render a tiny legend with 5pt width, but we get a large colourbar.

``` r
library(marquee)
library(ggplot2)

g <- ggplot(mtcars) +
  aes(x = mpg, y = hp, color = cyl) +
  geom_point() + 
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.text = element_marquee(), 
    legend.key.width = unit(5, 'pt')
  )
g
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/cOX9zoy.png)<!-- -->

With this PR

``` r
devtools::load_all("~/packages/test/marquee/")
#> ℹ Loading marquee
g
```

title: Marquee guide
description:
Hi Thomas,

This is my proposal for a marquee guide.
Instead of going into details, I'll render the examples which are hopefully somewhat self-expanatory.
Please let me know if you'd wish to change some things.

``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(marquee)
# A standard plot
base <- ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy)) +
  geom_point()

# Using key glyphs
base + aes(shape = drv) +
  scale_shape_discrete(
    # Same as using <<1>>, <<2>> and <<3>>,
    # or ![](1), ![](2) and ![](3)
    # or ![](4), ![](f) and ![](r)
    name = "Cars with four wheel <<4>>, forward <<f>> or reverse <<r>> drive.",
    guide = "marquee"
  )
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/e02uBSf.png)<!-- -->

``` r
# Recolouring text
base <- base +
  aes(colour = drv) +
  labs(
    colour = "Cars with {.4 four wheel}, {.f forward} or {.r reverse} drive."
  )
base + guides(colour = "marquee")
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/FBb5iMO.png)<!-- -->

``` r
# Adjust display of labels
st <- style(weight = "bold", italic = TRUE, background = NA)
base + guides(colour = guide_marquee(style = st))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/NXo6WsV.png)<!-- -->

``` r
# Using background instead of text colour by setting it to NULL
st <- style(color = "black", background = NULL)
base + guides(colour = guide_marquee(style = st))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/BV2XRPl.png)<!-- -->

``` r
# Customising style of each label through style sets
# Note: tag names must be universal per `vctrs::vec_as_names` and
# prefixed with `lab_`.
st <- classic_style()
st <- modify_style(st, tag = "lab_f", background = NULL, color = "black")
st <- modify_style(st, tag = "lab_r", border_size = trbl(1),
                   color = "black", background = NA)
base + guides(colour = guide_marquee(style = st))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/jxlxsnw.png)<!-- -->

``` r
# Alternatively:
base + guides(colour = "marquee") +
  theme(plot.subtitle = element_marquee(style = st))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/PuzUHel.png)<!-- -->

``` r
# Splicing in labels
base + aes(colour = class) +
  labs(colour = "Cars including !!2 and !!6 vehicles") +
  guides(colour = "marquee")
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/429Czfk.png)<!-- -->

``` r
# Using automatic detection
base + aes(colour = class) +
  labs(colour = "Cars including suv and minivan vehicles") +
  guides(colour = guide_marquee(detect = TRUE))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/IvuPR9y.png)<!-- -->

``` r
# Automatic detection is not always a good idea
base +
  labs(colour = "Kerfuffles 4 the riffraff from frankfurt") +
  guides(colour = guide_marquee(detect = TRUE))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/Wn3SIhC.png)<!-- -->

title: add `xDetails()`/`yDetails()` methods
description:
This PR aims to fix #11.

This was less complicated than anticipated, because the relevant corner points were already calculated somewhere.

Example from issue; the points on the bounding box are now found correctly:

``` r
devtools::load_all("~/packages/marquee/")
#> ℹ Loading marquee

label <- "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur 
adipiscing elit. In hendrerit metus quam, 
sed rutrum nulla feugiat consequat. Sed eu 
pulvinar purus, vel placerat metus."

theta <- seq(0, 315, by = 15)

mq <- marquee_grob(
  label, classic_style(), 
  angle = 45, x = 0.5, y = 0.5, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5
)

grid.newpage()
grid.draw(mq)

x <- grobX(mq, theta)
y <- grobY(mq, theta)

grid.points(x = x, y = y, gp = gpar(col = 'red'))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/0BgftfW.png)<!-- -->
